summary: 格莱泽在书中为城市辩护，指出人口集中方便人们交换想法、寻找机会，也更有利于创新。他认为限制市区建房会推高房价并促成郊区扩张，而依赖汽车的郊区生活往往带来更高的碳排放。
logic: 回顾崇尚乡村的反城市传统
解释密集城市如何交换思想
从贫困和房价讨论住房供应
用孟买与美国分析规划选择
比较城市与郊区的碳足迹

paragraphs.brief: 爱德华·格拉泽所著的《城市的胜利》 是一个令人激动的赞美诗赞美一个如此庞大和有效以至于它被普遍认为是理所当然的发明
sentences: Triumph of the City, by Edward Glaeser, is a thrilling and very readable hymn of praise to an invention so vast and so effective that it is generally taken for granted.
爱德华·格拉泽所著的《城市的胜利》 是一个令人激动的赞美诗赞美一个如此庞大和有效以至于它被普遍认为是理所当然的发明
More than half the global population already live in urban areas and, every month, five million more flood into the cities of the developed and developing worlds.
全球一半以上的人口已经生活在城市地区，每个月还有500万人涌入发达世界和发展中世界的城市。
The crowds and poverty of some of these modern cities may horrify us.
有些现代城市的人群和贫困可能使我们感到惊恐。
They shouldn’t, says Glaeser; they are signs of growth, energy and aspiration.
Glaeser说，他们不应该这样做；它们是增长、能量和愿望的迹象。
Cities are our best and brightest hope.
城市是我们最美好的希望。

paragraphs.brief: 19世纪的美国作家亨利·戴维·索罗撤退到瓦尔登庞德的荒野过着孤独、简单的生活并让几代美国人相信城市是坏的大自然是好的
sentences: This idea has had more than two hundred years of resistance.
这个想法有二百多年的抵抗力
Not long after the Industrial Revolution began in Britain, the Romantic poets turned away from the smoke and factories of their cities to celebrate the air and light of untouched nature.
在英国工业革命开始不久后，浪漫诗人们离开了城市的烟雾和工厂来庆祝空气和未触及自然的光芒

In 19th-century America, the writer Henry David Thoreau retreated to the wilderness of Walden Pond to live the solitary, simple life, and convinced generations of Americans that cities were bad and nature was good.
19世纪的美国作家亨利·戴维·索罗撤退到瓦尔登庞德的荒野过着孤独、简单的生活并让几代美国人相信城市是坏的大自然是好的

paragraphs.brief: Glaeser出色地描述了纽约停止发展到20世纪末作为世界文化和经济中心的地位。
sentences: They had, Glaeser admits, a point.
他们承认了，格拉泽承认了一点。
The early industrial cities were dirty, since they lacked efficient waste-disposal systems, and disease spread rapidly among the population.
早期的工业城市是肮脏的，因为它们缺乏有效的废物处理系统，疾病在人口中迅速蔓延。
But more importantly they were profitable, and there were enormous commercial incentives to make them work, as well as political ones.
但更重要的是，它们有利可图，并且有巨大的商业激励机制来使它们发挥作用，还有政治激励机制。

Their transformation could be achieved at a stroke: in the second half of the 19th century, the French Emperor Napoleon III gave Baron Haussmann unrestricted power to turn the slum-infested city of Paris into one of the wonders and delights of the modern world.
他们的转变可以一触即发：19世纪后半叶，法国拿破仑三世皇帝授予了豪斯曼男爵不受限制的权力，将受贫民窟侵袭的巴黎城市变成现代世界的奇迹和喜悦之一。
Or the transformation could be done by trial and error.
也可能是尝试和错误的转变
Glaeser gives a brilliant account of the stop-start progression of New York to its late 20th-century position as the cultural and economic centre of the world.
Glaeser出色地描述了纽约停止发展到20世纪末作为世界文化和经济中心的地位。
Either way, Paris, New York and other cities developed because they were truly effective markets of ideas and innovation.
不管怎么说，巴黎、纽约和其他城市都是发展起来的，因为它们是真正有效的思想和创新市场。

paragraphs.brief: 相反，城市应建造更多的房屋，从而控制地产价格。
sentences: For these and many other reasons, we should not be so upset by the spectacle of urban poverty.
出于这些原因和许多其他原因，我们不应对城市贫困的景象感到如此不安。
The poor flock to cities in the hope of becoming richer (which, by and large, they do).
贫穷的人聚集在城市里，希望自己变得更富(他们基本上也这样)。
They also reinvigorate the economy of the city.
他们还振兴了城市的经济。
It is folly to drive them away by forcing property prices to soar with unreasonable planning regulations.
强迫财产价格高涨，不合理的规划条例，将他们赶走是愚蠢的。
Instead, cities should build more houses and thereby hold property prices in check.
相反，城市应建造更多的房屋，从而控制地产价格。

paragraphs.brief: 这会在不破坏市中心布料的情况下，振兴市中心的大部分地方。
sentences: It can go wrong, of course.
当然会出错的
In Glaeser’s view, this is primarily because municipal authorities fail to understand the principal virtues of their cities.
Glaeser认为，这主要是因为市政当局不了解城市的主要优点。
The heart of Paris, as many Parisians say, is turning into a museum because of the desire to preserve Baron Haussmann’s 19th-century boulevards.
巴黎的中心，正如许多巴黎人所说，正变成一个博物馆，因为人们渴望保护Haussmann男爵的19世纪大道。
Glaeser defends their preservation, but argues that in the 1950s the French made a mistake in establishing a huge high-rise commercial development — La Défense — on the outskirts of the city.
Glaeser捍卫他们的保护，但争辩说，1950年代，法国人错误地在城市郊区建立了巨大的高层商业发展——“防御”。
Far better, he says, to have turned the central area of Montparnasse into a new commercial district.
他说，把蒙帕纳斯的中心地区变成一个新的商业区，这要好得多。
This would have revitalised much of the city centre without destroying its fabric.
这会在不破坏市中心布料的情况下，振兴市中心的大部分地方。
In India, Mumbai could save itself from ever-more inefficient sprawl over the surrounding area simply by relaxing the rules presently imposed on the height of new constructions.
在印度，孟买只要放松目前对新建筑高度所强加的规则，就能避免周围地区效率越来越低的无序扩张。

paragraphs.brief: 在美国，是郊区证明是真正的灾难。
sentences: In America, it is the suburbs that have proved to be the real disaster.
在美国，是郊区证明是真正的灾难。
Glaeser is repentant on this subject himself.
格拉泽在这件事上很悔改
He moved to the suburbs when he had children.
他有孩子时搬到郊区。
His entirely legitimate excuse is that the government made him (and millions like him) do it.
他完全合理的借口是政府让他(和数百万人一样)这么做。
By under-taxing petrol and imposing tight planning restrictions on inner cities that drove up the cost of property, it made flight to the suburbs more or less inevitable for the middle classes.
由于汽油税过低，对导致房地产成本上升的内城实行严格的规划限制，使中产阶级几乎不可避免地逃往郊区。

paragraphs.brief: 这是一场灾难，因为没有什么比郊区更低效的了。
sentences: This is a disaster because nothing is more inefficient than a suburb.
这是一场灾难，因为没有什么比郊区更低效的了。
Suburbanites mingle less, and lose the face-to-face contact that makes being an urbanite so much more creative.
郊区人混得少失去面对面的接触使得城市人更富有创意
Moreover, houses are costlier to heat and cool than flats, and suburbanites drive thousands more miles per year than city dwellers.
此外，房屋的热量和冷却程度比公寓还要高，郊区每年的车程比城市居民还要长几千英里。
Every aspect of life involves more consumption.
生命的每个方面都涉及更多的消费。
This leads to the strongest and newest argument in favour of cities — they are good for the environment.
这导致了有利于城市的最有力和最新的论据——城市对环境有利。
To live in the country or the suburbs is to have a vastly larger carbon footprint than any urbanite.
生活在乡下或郊区的碳足迹比任何城市居民都大得多。

paragraphs.brief: 如果你憎恨城市，对这个国家的思潮视而不见，不管怎样，格拉泽就是你要面对的人。
sentences: Full of characters and accessible information, this is a tremendous book, not least because, like me, you will find yourself constantly seeking reasons to disagree.
这本书充满了人物和可获取的信息，是一个巨大的书，特别是因为，像我一样，你会发现自己不断寻找理由来表达异议。
Like the poor in the city, this is a sign of success.
和城里的穷人一样这是成功的迹象
If you hate the city and get moist-eyed at the thought of the country then, one way or another, Glaeser is the man you will have to take on.
如果你憎恨城市，对这个国家的思潮视而不见，不管怎样，格拉泽就是你要面对的人。

items.en: Problems with early cities included dirt and ________.
items.zh: 早期城市的问题包括脏乱和________。
items.why: 早期城市除了脐脏以外的另一大问题就是疾病蔓延。

items.en: ____ (Q1) but there were commercial and ________ reasons for improving them
items.zh: 早期城市面临脏乱和________（Q1），而改善城市状况既有商业方面的原因，也有________方面的原因。
items.why: 除了商业动机，还有政治" 动机来促成改造。

items.en: Urban poverty is not a major problem because poor people generally get ________.
items.zh: 城市贫困并不构成大问题，因为穷人的生活通常会变得________。

他们能活跃城市的经济。

items.en: the centre of Paris is becoming a ________
items.zh: 巴黎市中心正在变成一座________。
items.why: 巴黎中心正变得像博物馆”一样死气沉沉。
市中心“房产” 价格高，使中产阶级逃离。

items.en: One disadvantage of the suburbs is less personal ________.
items.zh: 郊区生活的一个缺点是人与人之间的直接________较少。
items.why: 郊区生活缺少人与人之间面对面的“联系 / 接触”。

items.en: increased ________ of resources such as heating – which damages the environment
items.zh: 郊区生活增加了供暖等方面的资源________，从而损害环境。
items.why: 郊区生活在供暖等方面会导致更多“消耗”。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Glaeser believes that congestion and poverty in some modern cities indicate serious problems.
items.zh: 格拉泽认为，一些现代城市的拥挤和贫困表明存在严重问题。
items.why: Glaeser 认为拥挤和贫困是“增长与活力”的象征，而题干说它们是“严重问题"。

items.en: The writer Henry David Thoreau discussed the ideas of the Romantic poets in his work.
items.zh: 作家亨利·戴维·索罗在他的著作中讨论了浪漫诗人的想法。
items.why: 文中写梭罗隐居瓦尔登湖、追求简朴生活，没有介绍他在作品中是否讨论浪漫派诗人。

items.en: Emperor Napoleon III was influenced by the complaints of poor people living in Paris.
items.zh: 拿破仑三世皇帝受到生活在巴黎的穷人的投诉的影响。
items.why: 拿破仑三世授权奥斯曼改造巴黎，文中没有说这个决定受到贫民抱怨的影响。

items.en: Strict planning regulations may be beneficial for a city’s development.
items.zh: 严格的规划条例可能有利于城市的发展。
items.why: 作者认为不合理的规划限制会推高房价并赶走居民，因此不赞成它有利于城市发展的说法。

items.en: Glaeser argues that the location of commercial development at La Défense was a bad idea.
items.zh: Glaeser认为，商业发展的地点在国防部是一个坏主意。
items.why: Glaeser 明确认为把商业区建在 La Défense (郊外) 是“错误”,即地点选择不当。

points: 作者认为不合理的规划限制会推高房价并赶走居民，因此不赞成它有利于城市发展的说法。

先读主句的动作，再用 after 把这一层关系补进去。

“that cities were bad and nature was good”补足 convinced 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 convinced 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
